decision: Sign the 3-year exclusive supply agreement with Kestrel Optics

framing.context: Kestrel Optics is the only vendor shipping the 1.6um sensor stack our inspection head needs at our price point. They offered a 3-year agreement at 22% below list. In exchange we must buy 100% of sensor volume from them. The contract has no minimum capacity commitment on their side and no price protection past year one. Kestrel's other customer is a defense prime that outbids us and takes priority in any shortage. Our board wants the COGS cut booked before the Series A.
options: Counter: non-exclusive, 70% volume commitment, capacity SLA + price cap
Walk and qualify a second source (6 months, $180k NRE)

members.name: Alex
members.decisive_reason: The discount is real but we are buying it with the only leverage we have.

answers.P1_timing: Kestrel's quote expires 2026-08-21 but that is their sales-cycle deadline, not ours. Real cost of waiting 30 days is one quarter of margin, roughly $90k.
answers.P2_reversibility: 1-way. Exclusivity locks us out of qualifying anyone else for 3 years, and requalification takes 6 months even after the term ends.
answers.P3_expected_value: Base case: 22% COGS cut worth ~$1.4M over 3 years. Upside: Kestrel scales with us. Downside: a shortage year costs us a product launch.
answers.P4_downside_cap: Max loss is not the money, it is a missed Figure delivery window. That is survivable once, not twice.
answers.P5_opportunity_cost: $180k NRE and 6 months of a firmware engineer to dual-source. That engineer is otherwise on the ISP acceptance work.
answers.P6_information: The crux is whether Kestrel will put a capacity SLA in writing. We have never asked. One email, three days.
answers.P7_second_order: Exclusivity makes us a price-taker at renewal. It also tells the defense prime we are captive, which lowers their cost to squeeze us.
answers.P8_strategy_fit: Cutting COGS fits. Becoming dependent on a supplier whose bigger customer outranks us does not.
answers.P9_owner: I decide. Board is informed, not consulted, under $2M.
answers.P10_kill_criteria: If Kestrel misses two consecutive delivery windows in year one we should be able to exit. Today's draft has no such clause.

members.name: Jordan
members.decisive_reason: We do not have the cash or the headcount to run two supply chains.

answers.P1_timing: Decide now. Q3 build starts 2026-09-01 and long-lead parts need a PO.
answers.P2_reversibility: Practically 2-way. Contracts get renegotiated when volumes move.
answers.P3_expected_value: The 22% is banked cash. Shortage risk is maybe 20% in any given year.
answers.P4_downside_cap: Worst case we buy spot at list for a quarter. Painful, not fatal.
answers.P5_opportunity_cost: Dual-sourcing costs us the ISP acceptance schedule, which is the actual company-killer.
answers.P6_information: I want Kestrel's fab allocation numbers, but they will not share them.
answers.P7_second_order: A committed supplier ships us engineering samples first. That compounds.
answers.P8_strategy_fit: Yes. Cost discipline is how we survive to Series A.
answers.P10_kill_criteria: One missed window and we start qualifying a backup regardless of contract.
